title: PR gating: Long-tail latency exposure harness with stratified synthetic traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a CI-level harness that exposes PRs to long-tail latency effects and Token/s regressions using stratified synthetic traffic and an online baseline calibrator. This ticket builds a lightweight, reproducible runner that executes in PR CI, compares PR runs against a sliding production baseline, and fails PRs only on robust signals (statistical + delta thresholds). Goal is to catch regressions that only appear under realistic long-tail mixes (mixed prompt lengths, cache hit/miss, KV warmup) while minimizing false positives.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can be invoked from PR CI and completes within 8 minutes for standard quick suite
p95 comparison reports both absolute delta (ms) and relative effect size; CI failure triggers only when both exceed thresholds
Baseline is maintained as a 14-day sliding window and can be bootstrapped from nightly benchmark snapshots
Secondary throughput signal (tokens/sec) is reported and used as corroborating evidence in composite decision
Artifacts (raw latencies, token counts, traces) are uploaded to the runtime-performance dashboard and linked in PR results
tasks: Design stratified synthetic traffic mixes that model 3 buckets: short (<=32 tokens), medium (33-256), long (>256) with KV cache variations
Implement lightweight runner that executes inference traces against PR image and return latencies & token counts
Add online baseline calibrator service that fetches and summarizes last 14 days of nightly runs
Compute non-parametric 95% CI via bootstrap for observed p95; compute Cohen's d-like effect size for change magnitude
Integrate gate decision into GitHub Actions workflow with clear pass/fail output and artifact links
Create dashboard tile in runtime ops dashboard showing current baseline, recent PR runs, and alert history
Write onboarding docs and a short playbook for triaging false positives
technical_notes: Use stratified sampling so each run draws 200 traces per bucket (total 600 traces) to expose long-tail behavior without long run times
Bootstrap configuration: 1000 resamples on p95 metric; report median and 95% CI
Failure rule: absolute p95 increase >= 15ms AND relative increase >= 3% AND effect size estimate > 0.25 -> fail PR
Corroboration: if tokens/sec drops by >5% simultaneously, escalate severity; if throughput drops but p95 stable, mark as performance-quality tradeoff and annotate
KV-warmup: include a cold/half-warm/hot mix per bucket to simulate cache miss penalties; instrument KV hit-rate per trace
Baseline window: 14 days but require at least 10 valid nightly snapshots; fallback to last successful release snapshot if insufficient data
Fail-safe: allow an override tag [perf-ignore] on PRs for experimental forks; gating must be enabled by repo config flag
decisions: We will prefer non-parametric bootstrap over parametric models to avoid distributional assumptions on latencies
Composite decision requires both statistical significance (via CI/effect size) and a practical delta threshold to reduce noise
Use tokens/sec as a corroborating signal rather than primary gating metric to avoid rejecting tuned latency-for-throughput tradeoffs
Run harness in a standardized PR runner image (runtime-ci:v2) to reduce environment variability
